claims.text: Pre-existing short-range chemical order in equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles increases local atomic-diffusion activation barriers during high-temperature exposure.
The increased diffusion barriers caused by SRO stabilize the crystalline structure relative to a fully disordered state.
The increased diffusion barriers caused by SRO stabilize the chemical structure relative to a fully disordered state.
Rapid quenching produces a maximally disordered or random solid-solution state in 5–20 nm equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
Moderate annealing at approximately 600 K induces slight SRO in 5–20 nm equimolar CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles.
The proposed comparison holds composition, high-temperature exposure, atmosphere, and nominal stress conditions constant while varying the initial degree of SRO.
The relevant structural mediator is the magnitude and spatial distribution of SRO clusters together with correlated lattice-strain fields.
Thermally activated atomic diffusion drives local chemical reordering during the high-temperature treatment.
Favorable SRO clusters lower the system free energy.
SRO clusters locally modulate atomic-diffusion barriers.
SRO-mediated diffusion-barrier modulation suppresses extensive nanoparticle coarsening.
SRO-mediated diffusion-barrier modulation suppresses phase separation.
A fully disordered state permits uniformly higher atomic mobility than an SRO-containing state.
Higher atomic mobility in the disordered state causes greater coarsening and phase instability.
After treatment at 800–900 K for one hour, SRO-containing samples will coarsen less than rapidly quenched samples.
After treatment, SRO-containing samples will retain their lattice parameters better than rapidly quenched samples.
After treatment, SRO-containing samples will have a more uniform nanoparticle morphology than rapidly quenched samples.
The prediction is explicitly limited to 5–20 nm nanoparticles exposed at 800–900 K and may depend on the achieved SRO level.
Comparable diffusion barriers, comparable or greater coarsening, or failure to improve lattice-parameter retention in the SRO sample would falsify the proposed mechanism.
